description.p: nzbfast downloads from Usenet in one pass. Fetching, decoding, verifying, repairing and extracting all happen while the data is arriving rather than in separate stages afterwards, so a job is usually finished a moment after the last article lands.
It runs as a background program with a dashboard you open in your browser. Clicking the nzbfast icon starts it and opens that dashboard; closing the browser tab leaves it running.
It speaks the SABnzbd API, so Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Readarr and the usual phone apps talk to it without changes.

ul.li: Repairs and unpacks as the download arrives, including nested and split archives
Watches a folder for .nzb files, and takes them from your browser
Handles obfuscated and badly named posts
Shows what a file is before it has finished arriving

description.p: You need an account with a Usenet provider before nzbfast can download anything. It asks for those details the first time you open the dashboard.

This Flatpak package is a beta. The program inside it is the shipped release; the packaging is what is new, and a Flatpak can only reach the folders it has been granted. It comes with access to your home folder and the usual places removable and network drives are mounted. If you download somewhere else, grant it with Flatseal or flatpak override.
